newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom cuts mobile phone rates early.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom cuts mobile phone rates early.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG's mobile phone unit said on Monday it would bring forward the launch of its low-cost "Eco" package tariff by a week, making it available immediately to buyers.
DeTeMobil was the first of Germany's three mobile phone network operators to announce drastic price reductions recently -- but was later undercut by its competitors.
The company, which operates the D1 mobile phone network, said in a statement it was introducing the new tariffs early due to the "positive reaction from customers and market partners."

Under the new pricing structure, monthly rental fees for the Telly package will fall to 29 marks from 49 marks, while callers using the ProTel package will pay 15 percent less for daytime calls, DeTeMobil said in a statement.
All other prices remain unchanged under standard 24-month contracts. No minimum call volume or deactivation charges are set, DeTeMobil said.
Competitors Mannesmann Mobilfunk, operator of the D2 network, and third network operator E-Plus, have both trumped Telekom's initial price cuts.
E-Plus is owned by Veba, Thyssen, Bellsouth of the U.S. and Britain's Vodafone.
